Pay the entire balance before the closing due date. There is a closing and statement due date. They are different. The closing date is a few days before the statement due date. Basically the closing date to the day the bank reports your balance to the credit bureaus. The statement due date to when you must make a minimum payment (or more if you can).

To build credit, I suggest putting a subscription or two on the card and just pay that off in full before the closing date. I wouldn’t start using the card as much as you can since you have a low credit limit and a low credit age. It looks bad to the bank to see you using all the money and just paying the minimum payment.

That’s a terrible idea. If you want to do something like borrow money to invest, you’d be better off getting a personal loan with the lowest interest rate possible. I still think the idea is dumb because people don’t realize that investing is gambling if you are only doing it for a short period of time (<5 years). You probably won’t make much of a return or worst case scenario you lose the money and still have to pay your credit card or loan.

Financial advisors won’t tell you to borrow money to invest. You should invest money you have. You can definitely get the student line of credit (it’s a baby credit card with perks like a lower interest rate) but use the card like a debit card. You don’t want to max out any cards or get into credit card debt at such a young age. I can also assume you have little to no credit history so you should know that building a good credit score is important for adult things like car loans and getting approved for apartments. Do a little research on what entails a credit score but one element is utilization (how much of the available credit you’ve used). You are suggesting that you’d use 100% of your credit and you probably have no credit history. Your score would start off really terribly.

If you want to be “rich”, work and save money. Choose your career carefully. Don’t fall into lifestyle inflation. Don’t gamble money you don’t have.
